feedback: If the child gives a claim but no reason, prompt: 'What in the picture proves the beaver MADE the dam rather than found it?' (it placed the sticks).
If the child can't link to a need, offer the four needs (shelter, food, water, safety) and ask which one fits.
Praise a complete argument that names the action AND the need, and invite them to try the same for a second organism, including a plant or a person.
activities.intendedInsight: A simple evidence-based argument is a claim plus a 'because' that points to what the organism did and the need it meets.
learnerActions: Pick one organism from the habitat (beaver, bird, rabbit, tree roots, or a person).
State the claim out loud: 'This living thing changes its home.'
Give the reason: 'because it ____' (built a dam / gathered twigs / dug a burrow / its roots cracked the rock / built a house).
Add the need: 'so it has ____' (a safe pond / shelter for eggs / a place to hide / room to grow / shelter or food).
Use a 'claim + because' picture sentence frame to support speaking or drawing.
activities.title: Say the little argument: claim + because

feedback: Prompt at each find: 'What did the organism make? What does it use it for?'
If a child is unsure something was made rather than found, look for evidence of the action (gathered twigs, dug soil, roots pushing into stone, built walls or planted rows).
activities.intendedInsight: Organisms changing their habitats is real and all around us — by animals, plants and people — not just in pictures.
learnerActions: On a nature walk, spot real nests, burrows, root-cracked pavement or kerbs, and human-made changes such as houses, paths or gardens.
For each one found, name the organism (animal, plant or person), what it changed, and the need it meets.
Bring back one example to tell as a claim + because.
activities.title: Real-world nature walk complement
